sections.history: Ambar Perunthirukoil, at the place called Ambal (Ambar) in Tiruvarur district, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. It stands about 2 km west of the Ambar Makaalam temple, a separate Paadal Petra Sthalam of the same town. Counted among the Maadakoil temples attributed to Kochengat Chola, its stone shrine is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple with a three-tiered rajagopuram, the shrine enshrines Brahmapureeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Poonguzhalammai — also Sugandhakunthalambikai — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas within its walled enclosures. The form is that of the Maadakoil-style Shiva temples of the Tiruvarur delta.
sections.legends: The lord is worshipped as Brahmapureeswarar, the lord of Brahma's city: by tradition Brahma, having taken the form of a swan, bathed in the sacred well here and worshipped the lingam beside it, and was thereby relieved of a curse and restored to his own form. The goddess Poonguzhalammai stands beside him. The fuller sthala purana survives in local tradition and Sambandar's verses.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Tiruvarur delta include Ambar Perunthirukoil, with its neighbouring Ambar Makaalam, among their stops.
sections.experience: At Ambar Perunthirukoil the pilgrim comes to the lord of Brahma's city. Before Brahmapureeswarar and Poonguzhalammai, within the Maadakoil walls of the Tiruvarur delta, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple and the memory of Brahma freed of his curse at the sacred well.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Ambar Perunthirukoil lies at Ambal (Ambar), in Tiruvarur district, about 2 km west of the Ambar Makaalam temple. Nannilam and Tiruvarur are the nearest towns and rail heads, with buses and taxis to the village.
